newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums end steady in slow business.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums end steady in slow business.

text.p: Gas oil premiums were steady in thin volume on Tuesday with weakness from the closure of the Asian arb comfortably balanced by better demand, traders said.
"The market is illiquid, very small and very shallow," said one European gas oil trader.
IPE May and June futures were both $1 a tonne firmer at $166.75 and $166.25 respectively, boosted by better demand from unseasonably cool weather on both sides of the Atlantic.

A cargo of 0.2 percent heating oil moved at $4.75 over June IPE. Heating oil was later bid at a $5 premium to June and offered at $7 over. Low sulphur diesel cargoes were discussed at around June IPE +$13/15, unchanged to slightly firmer.
But several Russian cargoes loading in the next four days remain unclaimed and were being offered out with little success.
Low sulphur diesel barge premiums were steady at around May IPE +$11.50. Heating oil barges continued to be assessed variously at 25/75 cents over May IPE.

A tender by Germany's oil stocks agency for 250,000 tonnes of jet and 250,000 tonnes of diesel, was due to be awarded. But some suspected a second tender would be issued to enable the agency to obtain more suitable prices and locations.
